##### **Transcript**


This week is about two things. How do we capitalize on all this new capability that's growing exponentially? And 2nd, how do we build a capability inside of our organizations to deal with the consequences of all this capability that's growing exponentially? And in today's world, that means one singular thing, which is how do we collectively build out that frontier? Ecosystem, we need to be able to parlay all of this technological advances into real outcomes, new points of leverage for people, the organizations that we build as well as the society at large. That's the goal. And for us, that comes down to three things. One, keeping the human at the center of it all, ensuring that you have ownership. Over your organization's intelligence and learning and trust. And so our goal is to build a stack that addresses these three architectural imperatives. O let's start with Copilot. Copilot is the new operating system for work. We're excited to partner with Salesforce to bring Salesforce to Copilot. When you think about Copilot, it's been about the single player world. Time has come for a true multiplayer form factor where people, their agents and other people are driving towards that common goal with shared context. This is Copilot workspaces. And Foundry of course has all of the popular closed and open rate models. In fact today we are very excited to bring GD62 to Foundry. And today we are also announcing meters, latest models are all coming to Foundry as well. Our goal is to put additional points on the frontier curve really informed by these real world RE around task performance that matters to you. Inside of all the products and today we are thrilled to announce Microsoft Decision 1.1, which is now generally available and ready for enterprise deployment. We're introducing a new flagship family of agentic coding models, Code 2. You know, Code 2 is at the frontier of cost performance for everyday enterprise quoting tasks and we're taking the same approach with cyber as well. Today we are very excited about announcing Agent 365 Business Analytics. You can simply think of this as an ERP system or AI usage perception also helps essentially connect, you know the signals, the sensors, the actuators across all of the assets, right? You have identity, your client, your cloud, your apps, of course agents now and really secure your end to end environment. What a model tells us about itself is not even independent evidence and therefore cannot be trusted and one model monitoring another model. That's the same issue. So you essentially have these unacceptable nested set of black boxes which we now need to make transparent and verifiable. And that's why today we're also announcing the Microsoft AI Transparency Initiative. We are also we architecting of course the core compute, storage and networking primitives in Azure to execute, connect, share contacts at that agent scale. We're also reimagining the data layer and that's why we're building Horizon DB. Yeah, it's exciting. It's new distributed managed Postgres SQL database. It's 8X faster performance than self managed Postgres and today I'm excited to share that Horizon. B is generally available in Azure. And this next part is what I've been working on for I think 25 years of my life, which is we are bringing all of Horizon DVD into fabric. This represents the complete unification of transactional and analytical data for Agentic era. So that's just a very quick walk across all of the mayors of what we are building. This is the promise of the frontier ecosystem. And that's what we are focused on building together with you.

[Ashutosh Kumar](https://in.linkedin.com/in/ashutoshkumardatacenter?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 17h


Well said, Sir. A frontier ecosystem only matters when it works on the ground, not just on stage. In my daily work on data centres, I see this gap clearly. AI can show great promise in a demo, but real-world impact comes when power, cooling, connectivity and resilience all hold together under continuous load. When an AI system has to act, decide and execute, there is no room for downtime or latency. That is why this shift from models to real outcomes is so important. The value will not come from how advanced the model is alone, but from how reliably the infrastructure behind it can support it at scale, across different regions, languages and operating conditions like we have in India. Building that dependable layer is what will turn AI advances into actual productivity, and that is where the real work lies.

The one thing that struck while looking on this morning was how Microsoft was making itself a one stop shop to better compete. On a micro level, I created an AI Productivity and Workforce Transformation Programme™ with the intent to improve work processes and bridge the gap for those who can't pay or are not as knowledge using AI tools. As such it is also beginner friendly. I have about twelve tools in my Programme that also includes Microsoft Copilot, Excel AI, Word and Microsoft Forms. Looking at the presentation, I was amazed how Microsoft is competing with the Zapier's, Otter AI, Trello, Notion and others - kind of made me feel like I should rewrite the Programne using only Microsoft tools. However, that won't help many because my Programme tells people how to get things done using free AI tools until they can pay/ upgrade to the paid tools for greater, better results and collaboration. I was impressed by Microsoft's presentation today though👍🏼
